item: L3Harris runs the current FAA telecom network (FTI)
detail: Over 4,400 facilities on circuits leased from multiple local carriers it doesn't name. The 70% copper-to-fiber figure is confirmed: L3Harris's FTI page says 70% of sites were upgraded as of Nov. 2, 2026, and the FAA said on Nov. 5 that 69% of copper wires had been replaced. A cutover causing today's outage is unverified: no public cutover schedule or contract change names Nov. 13, and L3Harris says it switches over during carefully coordinated low-traffic windows, which a Friday afternoon peak does not fit. CBS, citing multiple sources, reports that an update to this L3Harris-operated network caused a reboot and crash; that is sourced reporting, not official confirmation, and an update is not the same as a copper-to-fiber cutover. L3Harris had no comment as of 6:46 PM ET, per CBS. Source pending: no public link found for a 2027 finish date. [L3Harris FTI](https://www.l3harris.com/all-capabilities/faa-telecommunications-infrastructure-fti) · [FAA Nov. 5 release](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-begins-retiring-decades-old-floppy-disks-air) · [L3Harris, May 2026](https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/editorial/2026/05/l3harris-reaches-over-50-faa-telecommunications-modernization) · [CBS Texas](https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/faa-ground-stop-halts-flights-at-dfw-and-dallas-love-field-airports/) A Saturday Hindustan Times explainer, citing Bloomberg, says L3Harris has been asked to diagnose the overload and that some equipment was already running over capacity; that stays Reported/unconfirmed, and L3Harris still has not issued a public comment as of Saturday morning. item: AT&T holds the next-generation FENS planning order
detail: FENS is not the network in service today. AT&T won the FENS contract in August 2026 (contract 693KA8-26-D-00016), but the only funded work is a $74.3M planning task order; Verizon moved to a supporting role. L3Harris still operates FTI. No recent public document names AT&T as a current FTI circuit provider, and nothing public links AT&T to today's outage. A Hacker News claim that AT&T provides the current ARTCC network is at most partly true and should not be confused with this planning order. Source pending: no public link found for today's 'no outage notice' or for user-report levels in the 2:45–4 PM window. item: Verizon's role on FENS, and its public network today
detail: Washington Technology says Verizon moved to a supporting role on the future FENS program, which is not the live FAA network. Separately, no Verizon public-network outage notice was found for the ground-stop window, and a minor Northeast data issue was reported as clearing around 1:51 PM, before the window. A contractor cut a backup fiber near Philadelphia, forcing the FAA onto backup systems and disrupting East Coast flights. Source note, not a silent correction: Reuters, CNBC and BBC say the FAA was already on a backup fiber while troubleshooting a primary circuit, and that an NJ Transit contractor then cut that backup near New Brunswick, N.J., leaving both lines down. That does not match this row's 'near Philadelphia' location or the idea that the cut forced the FAA onto backup.
